data.hypothesis: The previous target-local POPCNT candidate was valid and measured, but the catalog has only one distinct program and does not establish whether an unannotated builtin behaves similarly. This candidate removes target-specific attributes and uses __builtin_popcount under the unchanged frozen flags. If those flags do not enable POPCNT, GCC may lower the builtin differently; the separate official measurement will test whether the target-local annotation matters.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use the target-local result as a comparator, not as proof about the unannotated builtin.
memory_lessons.claim: The target-local candidate was correct on all six cases and measured 8.1893727e-05 seconds; the naive-bit-loop baseline was also correct and measured 0.00104609 seconds. These results do not compare target-local POPCNT with an unannotated builtin.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this candidate's official correctness and timing with the target-local candidate measured under the same protocol.

data.notes: This source isolates the unannotated builtin as a separately measured path. The prior target-local candidate is the available measured comparison; no new measurement or assembly inspection is claimed. The recurrence order, uint32_t accumulation, output overwrite, and threads parameter behavior are preserved.
transformations: Replaced the naive bit-loop helper with an unannotated helper using GCC __builtin_popcount.
Left the helper and run without target-specific POPCNT attributes and did not change global compiler flags.
Preserved the ordered j-then-i recurrence, uint32_t accumulation and wraparound, generic dimensions, output overwrite, and threads parameter behavior.
